name: Lunar Shapechanging
summary: Innate power (not a Charm): for 3 motes of Essence, a Lunar can assume the shape of any animal whose heart's blood she has drunk or lapped as it died.
mechanics: Simple dice action; the Lunar's player cannot split her dice pool for extra actions while using it. Reverting to the Lunar's last true form is reflexive and can happen even before the Exalt's initiative in the turn. For the heart's blood to count as tasted, the beast must die, the Lunar must kill it (or strike the killing blow if several Lunars take part in the hunt), and drink its blood as it dies. The animal changed into can be no smaller than a large housecat and no larger than an elk unless special Charms extend the size range. Lunars cannot shapeshift into constructs, Wyld offspring, or other humans, and cannot assume the shape of non-natural beasts. A Lunar who shifts into an animal gains its Strength, Stamina, natural attacks/abilities, and natural senses, but keeps his own Attributes and health levels if the animal is smaller/similar-sized; if larger or built for a different locomotion (flight, swimming), the Lunar keeps his own scale but gains the new mode of movement. Shapechanging into a beast form does not itself count against the number of Charms usable that turn, but 3 motes remain committed until the character returns to a true form.
notes: Chapter Five (Charms) preamble, 'Lunar Shapechanging' section. Distinct from the Shapechanging I Charm tree, which builds on this innate power.

name: True Forms
summary: A Lunar can have more than one 'true form.' Learning Finding the Spirit's Shape adds a totem animal as a second true form; learning Deadly Beastman Transformation on top of that adds a hybrid war-form as a third.
mechanics: Reversion between true forms (human, totem animal, hybrid) is not a Charm use and doesn't cost the Essence that was spent to enter that shape in the first place — the Lunar simply has multiple 'true' shapes. If the Lunar reverts to true form for any reason (usually spending Peripheral Essence), she assumes whichever of her true shapes she wore last.
compatibility: All Lunar castes; requires Finding the Spirit's Shape (totem form) and/or Deadly Beastman Transformation (hybrid form) to have more than one true form.
notes: 'True Forms' sidebar, same page as 'The Tell.'

name: The Tell
summary: Every Lunar has an unchanging physical oddity called the Tell, left over from the tattooing/scarification ritual that fixes her Caste. How severe the Tell is depends on how many times the character has purchased Deadly Beastman Transformation.
mechanics: 1-2 purchases of Deadly Beastman Transformation: small Tells (odd hair color, hair with a gray/black stripe, a discolored eyebrow, a prominent birthmark, a missing eye). More purchases: the Tell grows, often manifesting traits of the Lunar's favored (totem) animal — wolf ears, goat hooves, tiger-like paws, or blatant traits such as backward-bending fingers, extra eyes, or cyclopeanism. It is the nature of the Tell to try to conceal itself from those who don't know to look for it and reveal itself to those who do, an automatic effect of Exaltation, not something the character controls directly. A character who has not taken Deadly Beastman Transformation has a small Tell that conceals itself well. A Lunar whose Tell combines the traits of several animals (from changing totem animal) is known as a chimera.
notes: Suppressed at low anima-display levels by Hide of the Cunning Hunter, and up through the 4-7 mote anima level by Masking the Brilliant Form.

name: Fixing the Caste (Caste Mark tattooing)
summary: The trials that follow a young Lunar's Exaltation end once the No Moon overseeing them is satisfied of the newly-Exalted's caste. Once caste is confirmed, it is fixed for good via a ritual tattooing/scarification process performed by a No Moon.
mechanics: The tattooing ritual takes place under a moon of the young Lunar's caste; the ritual lasts three days and is painful. It is meant to endure for life and, once done, it's rarely too early for a Lunar to start learning to shapeshift. As the tattoos spread across the Lunar's body, the shifting of his Caste Mark slows and eventually stops. No two sets of tattoos are the same; the tattooing process is closer to writing a personalized prayer than replicating a tried-and-true passage verbatim, and requirements vary Lunar to Lunar. Regional/tribal styles vary the specific marks used (runic symbols in the North, geometric scars in the West, curving spiral-toned scars in the East, raised dots in the South).
compatibility: All Lunar castes; performed by a No Moon of the Silver Pact (or informally, if the young Lunar has no access to the Pact).
notes: Chapter Two, 'Fixing the Caste' section.

name: A Lunar Without a Caste
summary: Sidebar covering the consequences of a Lunar who is never given the caste-fixing tattoos: the Caste Mark keeps shifting with the moon, and the Lunar never learns the more powerful Charms available to a caste, though the lack of a caste doesn't endanger him in his own right.
mechanics: With too much exposure to the Wyld, an untattooed Lunar becomes gradually more and more unable to maintain his own shape. He may find shapeshifting easier as a whole, but he begins to shift involuntarily, whenever his mood changes. He begins to forget his original form and can no longer assume it as a reflex. This gradual loss of control tends to lead to lunacy, and from there, it's a short fall to becoming chimera. Staying away from the Wyld slows but doesn't stop this drift; the farther the young Lunar is from the Wyld, and the farther he is from any Lunars who might assist/protect him against the Realm's hunters, the more dangerous his situation becomes.
compatibility: Applies to any Lunar who has not undergone the caste-fixing tattoo ritual.
notes: 'A Lunar Without a Caste' sidebar box, same page as 'Fixing the Caste.'

name: Hide of the Cunning Hunter
summary: One of the first Charms young Lunars learn; suppresses the Lunar's Tell, making it effectively invisible under most circumstances.
requirements: Minimum Manipulation 1; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The effects of this Charm dissipate if the Lunar's anima banner reaches or exceeds the 4-7 motes level of display. Otherwise, it's impossible to detect the Lunar's tattoos/Tell, even for forms of sight that would perceive the effects of active Essence. Storytellers should assume individuals who see a Lunar with unsuppressed tattoos will regard the Lunar suspiciously for the purposes of perceiving his Tell, and most will immediately realize the character's nature.
notes: Shapeshifting Charms tree, first Charm (see Shapechanging I tree diagram, p. 124/PDF 127).

name: Masking the Brilliant Form
summary: Extends Tell-suppression so it works even while the Lunar's anima is active and blazing at the 4-7 motes display level.
requirements: Minimum Manipulation 2; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: Hide of the Cunning Hunter.
mechanics: While active, it is impossible to perceive the Tell of a Lunar who has never purchased Deadly Beastman Transformation. Lunars who have purchased Deadly Beastman Transformation 1-2 times are treated as if they had never purchased it for the purposes of having their Tells spotted. Lunars who have purchased Deadly Beastman Transformation 3+ times are treated as if they purchased it 1-2 times for the purposes of Tell-spotting. Effects end when the character's anima becomes more intense than the 4-7 motes level.
notes: Shapeshifting Charms tree, second Charm.

name: Finding the Spirit's Shape
summary: The Lunar chooses an animal no larger than an elk and no smaller than a large cat; that animal becomes her totem/spirit animal and its shape becomes a second true form.
requirements: Minimum Charisma 2; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: Reflexive; almost all Lunars know this Charm. A Lunar either tastes the heart's blood of her totem animal during initiation, or in many cases, finds the totem-shape when she Exalts. Such Exalts are driven by an incredible craving to consume the life of a beast of that species so they can fairly gain its form. If a Lunar wants a totem animal larger than a cat, she may fairly know it already; if smaller, she must know it before she can drink its blood to gain the shape. A Lunar may change her totem animal, but doing so is costly and dangerous: she must pay a dot of permanent Willpower and buy the Charm again. Traces of the previous totem form remain in the Lunar's Tell. A Lunar whose Tell combines the traits of several animals is a chimera and is regarded with scorn; in addition, the Lunar may offend the animal avatar of the species she forsakes.
notes: Shapechanging I tree. A Lunar in totem animal shape may spend 1 mote to activate this Charm and return to human shape; this may only be activated once per turn.

name: Deadly Beastman Transformation
summary: Shifts the Lunar into a monstrous human/totem-animal hybrid war-form, three feet taller than her normal height, mistakable for nothing but a sleek and deadly killing machine.
requirements: Minimum Charisma 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Finding the Spirit's Shape.
mechanics: This hybrid shape is one of the Lunar's true forms and includes many bonuses. The first time a character takes this Charm, she receives five Attribute points and two gifts, applied immediately after purchase; subsequent purchases each grant three Attribute points and one gift. A character can purchase this Charm no more times than she has points of Essence. Each Attribute point raises Strength or Stamina by 1, or two points raise Dexterity by 1; bonuses are fixed once allocated and cannot be saved up between purchases or moved later. These bonus Attributes count as natural Attributes for the purposes of Charms that double Attributes and of Charms that convert Attribute dice to automatic successes. Members of the Eclipse Caste may not learn this Charm, for it draws on a natural power of the Lunar Exalted that Solars cannot master or emulate.
compatibility: Duration: Instant. Type: Reflexive. Not available to Eclipse Caste.
notes: Purchasing this Charm increases the severity of the Lunar's Tell. Gifts granted by this Charm are listed under the Beastman Transformation Gifts table (p. 126/PDF 129).

name: Calling Luna's Favor
summary: Lets the Lunar manifest one of her Deadly Beastman Transformation gifts while still in human or totem (non-hybrid) form.
requirements: Minimum Manipulation 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Deadly Beastman Transformation.
mechanics: From immediately after activation until the end of the scene or until the character ends the Charm's effects, the Lunar enjoys the benefits of one of her Deadly Beastman Transformation gifts. The gift actually manifests and is an obvious mark of a supernatural character; it manifests regardless of whether or not it has prerequisite gifts.
notes: Shapechanging I tree.

name: Blossoming Gift of Luna
summary: Extension of Calling Luna's Favor that lets the Lunar retain a single manifested gift indefinitely, rather than only for a scene.
requirements: Minimum Charisma 4; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Calling Luna's Favor.
mechanics: By activating this Charm while in Beastman form, the Lunar may retain a single Deadly Beastman Transformation gift until she ends the Charm's effects or next enters hybrid form. As with Calling Luna's Favor, the gift actually manifests and is in no way concealed; it manifests regardless of whether the gift has prerequisites.
notes: Shapechanging I tree.

name: Towering Beast Form
summary: Knowledge-only Charm (no activation cost) that enhances the Lunar's hybrid war-form, letting it scale up to as large as a Tyrant Lizard or other large dinosaur, rather than being capped at elk-size.
requirements: Minimum Charisma 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Finding the Spirit's Shape.
mechanics: There is no cost to use this Charm's effects — simply learning it enhances the Lunar's capabilities passively. Members of the Eclipse Caste may not learn this Charm, for it draws on a natural power of the Lunar Exalted that Solars cannot master or emulate.
compatibility: Duration: Indefinite. Type: Special. Not available to Eclipse Caste.
notes: Shapechanging I tree; distinct branch from Deadly Beastman Transformation.

name: Horrifying Might (Beastman Transformation gift)
summary: Sample Deadly Beastman Transformation gift giving unparalleled command of the Lunar's body, muscles as strengthened as if transformed into steel hawsers, agility to match that of a monkey.
requirements: Selected as one of the gifts granted by a purchase of Deadly Beastman Transformation.
mechanics: Grants +2 Attribute points if taken with the first purchase of Deadly Beastman Transformation, or +1 if taken with a subsequent purchase of the Charm. These points may only be spent on physical Attributes (Strength, Dexterity, Stamina). May only be taken once.
notes: Beastman Transformation Gifts table; Charms can mimic gift effects per the table's introduction, and Storytellers/players may develop other gifts beyond this sample list.

name: Bestial Reflexes (Beastman Transformation gift)
summary: The Lunar moves with bestial speed, raising base initiative.
requirements: Selected as one of the gifts granted by a purchase of Deadly Beastman Transformation.
mechanics: Increases base initiative by +3. May be taken up to two times (maximum +6).
compatibility: Prerequisite for Spider-Foot Climbing (alongside Lightning Speed).
notes: Beastman Transformation Gifts table.

name: Lightning Speed (Beastman Transformation gift)
summary: Doubles the character's running and jumping distances.
requirements: Selected as one of the gifts granted by a purchase of Deadly Beastman Transformation.
mechanics: Bonuses operate on the unmodified numbers. If the character is a Full Moon with her anima activated, running speed is tripled rather than merely doubled.
compatibility: Prerequisite for Spider-Foot Climbing (alongside Bestial Reflexes).
notes: Beastman Transformation Gifts table.

name: Spider-Foot Climbing (Beastman Transformation gift)
summary: The Lunar can move at half normal speed across any surface, however slick, including vertical or upside-down surfaces.
requirements: Selected as one of the gifts granted by a purchase of Deadly Beastman Transformation. Prerequisite gift: Bestial Reflexes or Lightning Speed.
mechanics: The character may not stop moving while off the horizontal, or he will fall normally. The character can bear loads of up to (Strength x 50 pounds) through the use of this gift.
notes: Beastman Transformation Gifts table.

name: Glue-Foot Climbing (Beastman Transformation gift)
summary: The Lunar can scuttle with preternatural speed up walls and across ceilings, and may stop and hang in any orientation without fear of falling.
requirements: Selected as one of the gifts granted by a purchase of Deadly Beastman Transformation. Prerequisite gift: Spider-Foot Climbing.
mechanics: The character can support loads of up to (Strength x 100 pounds) through the use of this gift.
notes: Beastman Transformation Gifts table.

name: Gift of Hands (Beastman Transformation gift)
summary: The character grows one or two extra arms, or other manipulative extremities such as trunks or tails.
requirements: Selected as one of the gifts granted by a purchase of Deadly Beastman Transformation.
mechanics: The character can hold things normally, wield extra weapons, and more easily do several things at once; the penalty for multiple actions is reduced by -1 for each extra action (never below -0), but the character still cannot split her dice pool for extra actions during any turn in which she is under the effects of an extra-action-type Charm. Characters do not enjoy the benefits of this gift during any turn in which they are under the effects of an extra-action-type Charm during their initiative.
notes: Beastman Transformation Gifts table.

name: Arm-Array (Beastman Transformation gift)
summary: The character has more than two arms — as few as three, or possibly as many as 30 — able to hold many weapons at the ready.
requirements: Selected as one of the gifts granted by a purchase of Deadly Beastman Transformation. Prerequisite gift: Gift of Hands.
mechanics: The character pays the attunement cost for each magical weapon individually. The character's dice-pool penalty from multiple actions is reduced by -3 for each extra action (it cannot go below -0), but the player still cannot split her dice pool for extra actions during her initiative under this gift. Characters do not enjoy the benefits of this gift during any turn in which they are under the effects of an extra-action-type Charm.
notes: Beastman Transformation Gifts table.

name: Terrible Beast Claws (Beastman Transformation gift)
summary: The Lunar's claws and bite become natural weapons.
requirements: Selected as one of the gifts granted by a purchase of Deadly Beastman Transformation.
mechanics: Claws: Spd +3, Acc +1, Dmg +3L, Pry +1. Bite: Spd +0, Acc +2, Dmg +5L, Pry +0. A Lunar gets both claws and bite from this gift. Attacking with these natural weapons is a Brawl or Martial Arts attack, whichever the Lunar prefers.
notes: Beastman Transformation Gifts table.

name: Savage Moonsilver Talons (Beastman Transformation gift)
summary: The Lunar's fangs and claws grow huge and moonsilver-capable, carving through flesh, bone, or metal with equal ease.
requirements: Selected as one of the gifts granted by a purchase of Deadly Beastman Transformation. Prerequisite gift: Terrible Beast Claws.
mechanics: Claws: Spd +6, Acc +4, Dmg +5L, Pry +4. Bite: Spd +3, Acc +2, Dmg +8L, Pry +0. The character has some control over the fangs and claws and can adapt them to meet his needs (for example, lengthening them to rend flesh or retracting them to allow him to handle objects unimpeded), though the stats remain the same. The Lunar's moonsilver talons and teeth can harm dematerialized spirits and count as moonsilver weapons for the purposes of Charms that affect those items.
notes: Beastman Transformation Gifts table.

name: Resilience of Nature (Beastman Transformation gift)
summary: The Lunar heals quickly while in hybrid form.
requirements: Selected as one of the gifts granted by a purchase of Deadly Beastman Transformation.
mechanics: Heals 1 Bashing point per turn, or 1 Lethal point per hour, while in hybrid form. This healing takes place at the start of the turn, is a reflexive action, and does not count against the Lunar's actions. No dice rolls are required.
notes: Beastman Transformation Gifts table.

name: Humble Mouse Shape
summary: Knowledge-only Charm that lets the Lunar shapeshift into forms smaller than a cat, down to as small as a field mouse.
requirements: Minimum Charisma 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Finding the Spirit's Shape.
mechanics: There is no cost to use this Charm's effects — learning it simply enhances the Lunar's capabilities. Members of the Eclipse Caste may not learn this Charm, for it draws on a natural power of the Lunar Exalted that Solars cannot master or emulate.
compatibility: Duration: Indefinite. Type: Special. Not available to Eclipse Caste.
notes: Shapechanging II tree.

name: Shaping the Ideal Form
summary: Lets the Lunar make cosmetic changes to the appearance of any of her true forms.
requirements: Minimum Manipulation 2; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: Finding the Spirit's Shape.
mechanics: Modifications include changing hair, eye, or skin color by several shades, lengthening or shortening hair length, and reshaping a chin or nose slightly or straightening teeth. A modification only applies to the form in which it was used — altering hair color in both human and totem-animal shapes requires using the Charm twice. Shaping the Ideal Form does not allow the Lunar to assume the appearance of another being, though it may help disguise his appearance; Lunars who wish to assume the form of specific individuals must instead use the Charm Prey's Skin Disguise. Shaping the Ideal Form cannot be used to conceal the Lunar's Tell or tattoos. No matter how much effort is put into the shaping, the Charm cannot be used to improve the Lunar's Physical Attributes unless the player invests experience in raising the Attribute — in that case, training time can represent an extended campaign of cosmetic self-improvement by reshaping. Overuse of the Charm tends to detract from the Lunar's appearance, rendering him bland, and is regarded as a sign of degeneracy and vanity among Luna's Beloved.
notes: Shapechanging II tree root Charm; also a prerequisite for the entire Body Enhancement and Shapechanging III cascades.

name: Many-Faced Moon Transformation
summary: Changes the gender the Exalt presents through any of her true forms.
requirements: Minimum Charisma 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Shaping the Ideal Form.
mechanics: Males become females and vice versa through their personalities, knowledge, and Traits unchanged. This is not a cosmetic modification — the Charm changes the Lunar's biology, and he or she becomes capable of siring or bearing children in either sex. While many Lunars have a preferred gender, individual Lunars have a 'natural' sex — they're considered to be in true form in either gender. Attempts by a pregnant Lunar to use this Charm automatically fail. Members of the Eclipse Caste may not learn this Charm, for it draws on a natural power of the Lunar Exalted that Solars cannot master or emulate.
compatibility: Duration: Instant. Type: Reflexive. Not available to Eclipse Caste.
notes: Shapechanging II tree.

name: Prey's Skin Disguise
summary: Lets the Lunar assume the outward appearance of a specific other human she has consumed.
requirements: Minimum Charisma 4; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Towering Beast Form, Humble Mouse Shape, Many-Faced Moon Transformation.
mechanics: The Lunar must consume the target's heart's blood to gain this appearance. She gains the victim's outward appearance and Physical Attributes and Appearance, but not the victim's knowledge, Mental or Social Attributes, or Abilities. If the target is an Exalt, the Lunar gains his outward appearance but remains a Lunar. This Charm cannot be used to mimic the Fair Folk, who, though humanoid, are something other. The character can still dress and act any way she desires — she adopts the victim's outward appearance, not personality. A Lunar willing to consume many mortals can develop quite a diverse catalog of shapes. As with any other type of shapechanging, the appearance of the character's Tell and tattoos is unchanged. Lunars who wish to masquerade as the persons they consumed would thus be well-advised to use Charms to suppress those unmistakable signs. Members of the Eclipse Caste may not learn this Charm, for it draws on a natural power of the Lunar Exalted that Solars cannot master or emulate.
compatibility: Duration: Indefinite. Type: Simple. Not available to Eclipse Caste.
notes: Shapechanging II tree.

name: Lunar Blood Reshaping Technique
summary: By having a willing subject taste the Lunar's blood, the Lunar can make minor alterations to that subject's form.
requirements: Minimum Manipulation 4; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Shaping the Ideal Form.
mechanics: The range of possible changes are as per Shaping the Ideal Form — this Charm cannot be used to change a target's shape to a specific person's or to give her the appearance of another human. Unlike modifications the Lunar makes to himself, the changes fade after a day. The subject must also spend a temporary Willpower point (two if she is an Exalt). Unwilling subjects, tattooed Lunars, non-humans, the undead, and unmaterialized spirits cannot be shaped by this Charm. Once the Charm is activated, the player rolls Manipulation + Craft (Body Shaping) at standard difficulty. One success or more indicates success, while if the roll fails, the subject's form is unaltered. A botch, however, results in an unexpected — and usually unpleasant — outcome.
notes: Shapechanging II tree; the health-level cost is described in the following (Wondrous Lunar Transformation) and Shaping the Once-Living Form entries as coming from the subject smearing/tasting the Lunar's blood.

name: Wondrous Lunar Transformation
summary: A more powerful version of the Lunar Blood Reshaping Technique, allowing the Lunar to alter a subject's form to match one of the patterns in the Lunar's 'library.'
requirements: Minimum Manipulation 5; Minimum Essence 4; Prerequisite Charms: Prey's Skin Disguise, Lunar Blood Reshaping Technique.
mechanics: This process is difficult and painful for the subject and requires immense skill by the Lunar, but it allows the subject to attain a non-human form or to masquerade as another human. In addition to the costs to the Lunar, the subject must spend 2 temporary Willpower points (3 if an Exalt). Unwilling subjects, tattooed Lunars, non-humans, the undead, and unmaterialized spirits cannot be shaped by this Charm. Once the Charm is activated, the Lunar's player rolls Manipulation + Craft (Body Shaping) at difficulty 3. Three or more successes indicates success, while if the roll fails (or gets only one or two successes), the subject's form is unaltered. A botch, however, results in an unexpected — and usually unpleasant — outcome, probably a subject twisted and crippled for the duration or possibly suffering permanent damage.
notes: Shapechanging II tree.

name: Shaping the Once-Living Form
summary: Lets the Lunar reshape inert, once-living material (wood, bone) into another form — a weapon, a piece of armor, or clothing.
requirements: Minimum Manipulation 3; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Lunar Blood Reshaping Technique.
mechanics: The Lunar cannot use this Charm to create complex objects with moving parts (a simple buckle is about as sophisticated as it gets), nor can it be used to reshape objects that are already under the influence of Charms, sorcery, or other supernatural effects. The item to be shaped must be smeared with the Lunar's blood, costing him a single health level (unsoakable lethal damage) before Essence can be channeled into the object. The texture and appearance of the original material remains unaltered (a wood weapon is always still wood, not metal), though the product may be modified by conventional means (dyes, paint, and so forth). The Essence cost of the Charm reflects the amount of raw material affected. If the target object is roughly the same size as the raw material, the Essence cost of the Charm is unaltered. If a size change is part of the process, the Lunar must spend additional Essence motes allowing the final product's size to be twice (or half) that of the raw material. An object fashioned in this manner is not permanent, but rather remains the Lunar commits the Essence. If the Lunar uses the Essence for other purposes, the product reverts to original form. A Lunar can, however, make his construct permanent by spending a point of Willpower, but he may only do so at the moment of creation. In this case, the Charm is instant, and the Essence returns normally. Shaping the object requires a Manipulation + Craft roll, usually of difficulty 1. The Storyteller may, however, increase this difficulty for more complex shapes. This Charm cannot effect the undead.
cost: 1 mote per raw cubic foot, 1 per volume increase + 1 health level
notes: Shapechanging II tree; description continues onto the next page (printed 131/PDF 134), which opens the Shapechanging III tree.

name: Fish Tail Technique
summary: Transforms the Lunar's limbs to enhance swimming: turning limbs into flippers, webbing hands and feet, or similar effects.
requirements: Minimum Charisma 3; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Shaping the Ideal Form.
mechanics: Using this Charm, a Lunar transforms his limbs to enhance his swimming abilities, turning his limbs into flippers, webbing hands and feet or performing other similar effects (at the Lunar's discretion) to enhance his swimming abilities, allowing him to move through water unimpeded at twice his normal movement rate. If he is in a form with innate swimming abilities, such as if a shark or a seal, this Charm confers no additional benefits. This Charm does not confer the ability to breathe water, and the character must surface to breathe (per the holding breath rules on p. 243 of Exalted) or risk drowning.
notes: Shapechanging III tree.

name: Tool-Hand Technique
summary: Lets a Lunar reshape her hands and fingers into the shapes of tools for craft tasks, without needing prefabricated tools.
requirements: Minimum Manipulation 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Shaping the Ideal Form.
mechanics: Most Lunars abhor the trappings of civilization, but this does not mean that they don't occasionally require tools. Unlike mortals, who must keep a range of prefabricated tools for such circumstances, a Lunar can reshape his body to provide the necessary instruments. Hands are strengthened and fingers and claws sharpened and reshaped to provide any tool the Exalt might need. While using the Tool-Hand Technique, the Lunar can naturally perform tasks that would normally require tools (for example, boring a hole in wood, hammering a peg or picking at stone). The Lunar's hands, feet or whatever else is shaped into the tool takes on a superficial resemblance to the tool in question but remains indisputably flesh and bone (albeit flesh and bone surrounded by a nimbus of Essence). A Lunar with multiple limbs can equip multiple limbs at a cost of 1 mote per limb and suffers no injury from the pounding, cutting or rasping of using the 'tools.' The Tool-Hand Technique cannot be used to form weapons or to otherwise give the Lunar an advantage in inflicting or withstanding damage, nor does the Lunar work faster than she would with normal tools. Any rolls involving Craft gain +2 dice when the Lunar uses this Charm.
notes: Shapechanging III tree; description continues onto the next page (printed 132/PDF 135).

name: Rat-Head Technique
summary: Deforms the Lunar's bones, muscles, and organs to squeeze through gaps far too small to normally fit through.
requirements: Minimum Manipulation 2; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Shaping the Ideal Form.
mechanics: By means of this Charm, the Lunar can squeeze his bones, muscles and organs capable of immense deformation, allowing him to squeeze through gaps it would not normally fit. By means of this Charm, a human-sized Lunar could wriggle through a hole as small as a mouse hole or a knothole in a fence. The process is very unsettling to watch and is likewise uncomfortable for the Lunar. The Rat-Head Technique cannot be used as part of any Combo or while the Lunar is under the effects of a Charm or sorcery that hardens or reinforces his limbs in any manner (such as the Body Weapon Technique). While using this Charm, the Lunar's natural soak cannot exceed 2B/2L under any circumstances, and he cannot parry lethal attacks without an appropriate stunt — his 'softened' body lacks the strength to do so effectively. A Lunar under the effect of Rat-Head Technique may dodge normally.
notes: Shapechanging III tree.

name: Ox-Body Technique
summary: Lets the Lunar buy extra health levels as if it were a Charm, purchasable once per dot of human-form Stamina.
requirements: Minimum Stamina: varies; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: The bodies of the Exalted are far more durable than those of mere mortals. To help simulate this, an Exalt may buy extra health levels as if they were a Charm. A player may purchase this Charm up to once per dot of human-form Stamina his character possesses. Each Ox-Body Technique Charm purchased can provide two -1 health levels or four -2 health levels, at the player's option, determined at the time of purchase.
notes: Opens the Body Enhancement Charms section and its Body Enhancement I tree; not itself part of the tree diagram.

name: Crouching Tiger Exercise
summary: A preparation ritual that lets the Lunar temporarily boost his Strength.
requirements: Minimum Charisma 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Shaping the Ideal Form.
mechanics: Lunars employ Essence to enhance their muscles via this Charm, using a series of stances and static exercises to focus Essence into their limbs, increasing their strength and resilience. A Lunar using this Charm swells into an intimidating, muscular brute. Her tendons stand out like taut rope, and her muscles seem ready to burst through her skin. The Exalt's player makes a Strength + Athletics roll. For every success, add one to the Lunar's Strength. That character cannot more than double her initial Strength through the use of this Charm. This is a dice bonus added by a Charm and should be considered as such when determining the maximum effect of other dice-bonus Charms. The Charm's effects last for a number of turns equal to the character's Essence + the number of success rolled. The exercises used to activate the Crouching Tiger Exercise require the character's undivided dice action for a number of turns equal to 10 + (the Lunar's Strength prior to the performance of this exercise). These turns of preparation must be concurrent and uninterrupted and cannot be combined with the preparation periods of other, similar exercises.
notes: Body Enhancement I tree.

name: Moonsilver Monkey Exercise
summary: A preparation ritual, parallel to the Crouching Tiger Exercise, that lets the Lunar temporarily boost his Dexterity.
requirements: Minimum Charisma 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Shaping the Ideal Form.
mechanics: By performing a series of limbering-up exercises and stances as he directs Essence through his muscles, a Lunar Exalt can temporarily boost his hand-eye coordination, his movements becoming fluid and graceful as moonsilver. The Exalted's player makes a Dexterity + Athletics roll. For every success, add one to the Lunar's Dexterity. That character cannot more than double his initial Dexterity through the use of this Charm. This is a dice bonus added by a Charm and should be considered as such when determining the maximum effect of other dice-bonus Charms. The Charm's effects last for a number of turns equal to the character's Essence + the number of success rolled. Enacting the Moonsilver Monkey Exercise requires the character's undivided action for a number of turns equal to (the Lunar's Dexterity prior to the performance of this exercise) + 10. These turns of preparation must be concurrent and uninterrupted, and cannot be combined with the preparation periods of other, similar exercises.
notes: Body Enhancement I tree; description continues onto the next page (printed 134/PDF 137).

name: Regaining Breath Exercise
summary: Lets the Lunar draw on his strength of spirit to fortify and regain Essence.
requirements: Minimum Intelligence 4; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Crouching Tiger Exercise, Moonsilver Monkey Exercise.
mechanics: In addition to using his Essence to fortify his body, a Lunar can draw on his strength of spirit to fortify Essence. By entering a trance and focusing his mind inward for a number of turns equal to (20 - his Stamina), a Lunar can regain motes of Essence via a Stamina + Endurance roll. For every success, the Lunar regains 2 motes of Essence. The character cannot regain more than his normal maximum temporary Essence, nor can he regain more than (his permanent Essence x 2) motes per use of the Charm. These turns of concentration must be concurrent and uninterrupted and cannot be combined with the preparation periods of other, similar exercises.
notes: Body Enhancement I tree.

name: Breath-Drinking Executioner Attack
summary: Lets the Lunar trap and consume the vital energy released by a slain individual to restore her own Essence reserves.
requirements: Minimum Wits 4; Minimum Essence 4; Prerequisite Charms: Regaining Breath Exercise.
mechanics: The death of an individual releases the target's lower or 'animal' soul, from which the Lunar can trap and consume vital energy to restore her Essence reserves. By means of the Breath-Drinking Executioner Attack, a Lunar can trap and consume this vital energy to restore her Essence reserves. By activating the Charm immediately after slaying an opponent, a Lunar regains the result of one 10-sided die in motes of Essence. An Exalt cannot regain more Essence in a given turn than she has points of Stamina.
notes: Body Enhancement I tree, terminal Charm.

name: Predator Grace Method
summary: Grants the Lunar premature balance beyond even the greatest feline.
requirements: Minimum Dexterity 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Shaping the Ideal Form.
mechanics: The Exalt can walk across surfaces as fragile as bamboo and string with ease and easily resists efforts to unbalance him. By spending motes of Essence, the Lunar's player may convert Dexterity dice into automatic successes when making a single Athletics roll to resist or resist balance and climbing or resist sweeps, clinches, holds or tackles. Upon activating the Charm, the Lunar's body and features undergo subtle changes, resulting in a lithe and graceful appearance that shifts to give him the best balance and grip possible in the present circumstances. The Lunar may not exceed his normal maximum temporary Essence through the use of this Charm.
notes: Body Enhancement II tree root Charm.

name: Panther Stride Stance
summary: The Lunar's legs shift into the likeness of the legs of a giant cat, greatly increasing running and leaping speed for a scene.
requirements: Minimum Manipulation 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Predator Grace Method.
mechanics: Using this Charm, the Lunar's legs shift into the likeness of the legs of a giant cat, and his whole body twists, slightly becoming lower and more streamlined. For the remainder of the scene, the Lunar can move at twice his normal movement rate and leap three times his normal jumping distance. If the target surface is uncertain, the Lunar's player must still make a (Dexterity or Wits) + Athletics roll to land successfully after such a leap (see p. 252 of Exalted). A Lunar may carry a 'passenger' on such a leap, doing so reduces his effective Dexterity by one and his effective Strength by two. A Full Moon who uses this Charm in conjunction with his anima power moves at three times his normal movement rate and leaps five times his normal jumping distance.
notes: Body Enhancement II tree.

name: Cat-Falling Attitude
summary: Greatly improves the Lunar's ability to avoid damage from a fall.
requirements: Minimum Dexterity 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Predator Grace Method.
mechanics: Using this Charm, a Lunar greatly improves his ability to avoid damage from a fall. He will always land on his feet and suffers only one level of bashing damage for every 10 feet fallen. Furthermore, he only suffers lethal damage if he falls more than 100 feet or onto a treacherous surface such as spikes.
notes: Body Enhancement II tree. The rendered page did not show a legible 'Cost:' line for this Charm (Duration/Type/Minimums were legible); re-render/re-check this specific entry at higher zoom before promotion to confirm its mote cost.

name: Flying Tiger Technique
summary: Creates a flap of skin between the Lunar's arms and legs, drastically extending her leaping ability into gliding.
requirements: Minimum Manipulation 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Panther Stride Stance.
mechanics: By creating a flap of skin between his arms and legs, a Lunar can drastically extend his leaping abilities. Using the skin flap as crude gliding wings, a Lunar using this technique can extend his horizontal leaping distance in excess of 10 times his normal leaping distance, though this depends on his trading height for distance. He can travel 20 yards per dot of Strength and Athletics, and another two yards for every yard of altitude he descends. For example, a Lunar with Strength 3, Athletics 3 who leaps from a branch 100 yards up may glide to a point on the ground 320 yards away ([3 x 20] + [3 x 20] + [2 x 100] yards). The Lunar may attempt to extend this distance by rolling Dexterity + Athletics, each success adding 10 percent to the range. The anima powers of a Full Moon Lunar and other movement-enhancing Charms do not add to the gliding distance of the Skin-Flap Flying Method.
notes: Body Enhancement II tree. The book refers to this Charm's effect internally as the 'Skin-Flap Flying Method' in its own description.

name: Tree-Dwelling Jaguar Claws
summary: Lets the Lunar grow and adapt claws to grip trees (or other surfaces where claws can grip) with surprising ease.
requirements: Minimum Dexterity 3; Minimum Essence 3; Prerequisite Charms: Shaping the Ideal Form.
mechanics: Using his protean abilities to grow claws and to adapt his skeleton and muscles, a Lunar Exalted can ascend trees (or other surfaces where his claws can grip) with surprising ease. A Lunar normally uses half his movement rate when climbing but may use his full movement rate without penalty if his player makes a successful Dexterity + Athletics roll. When faced with difficult climbing conditions (high winds, overhangs, etc.), a Lunar using this Charm reduces the difficulty of the Dexterity + Athletics rolls by 1 (but not below 1). If the Lunar makes unarmed Brawl or Martial Arts attacks while the Charm is active, his attacks inflict lethal damage.
notes: Body Enhancement II tree.

name: Cat Paw Climbing Style
summary: Lets the Lunar ascend, descend, or traverse any surface with relative ease, even if there are no obvious handholds.
requirements: Minimum Dexterity 4; Minimum Essence 4; Prerequisite Charms: Tree-Dwelling Jaguar Claws.
mechanics: Using this Charm, a Lunar may ascend, descend or traverse any surface with relative ease, even if there are no obvious handholds. Instead, he relies on minute adjustments to his fingers and toes to exploit minute variations in surface texture. The Lunar may move up to half his normal movement rate either horizontally or vertically, and reduces the difficulty of all Dexterity + Athletics rolls by 2 (but not below 1). Lunar characters may carry up to 100 pounds per point of Strength while using this Charm.
notes: Body Enhancement II tree; description begins at the bottom of printed p. 135 (PDF 138) and continues onto printed p. 136 (PDF 139), which opens the Unarmed Combat Charms section.

name: Body Weapon Technique
summary: Enhances the Lunar's unarmed-combat blows by focusing Essence into his limbs, making an unarmed attack inflict lethal rather than bashing damage.
requirements: Minimum Strength 1; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: None.
mechanics: A Lunar may use this Charm to enhance his unarmed-combat abilities, making his blows more deadly by focusing Essence into his limbs. Rather than inflicting bashing damage when executing a single unarmed Brawl or Martial Arts attack (not a wrestling maneuver), his blow causes lethal damage.
notes: Root Charm of the Unarmed Combat I, II, and III trees, and of the separately-diagrammed Combat cascade including Subduing the Honored Foe and Bull Head Technique (not yet inventoried).

name: Sinuous Striking Grace
summary: Uses Essence flows to suggest the likely actions of allies and enemies, letting the Lunar improve her initiative.
requirements: Minimum Dexterity 1; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: Body Weapon Technique.
mechanics: The Lunar uses Essence flows to suggest the likely actions of allies and enemies alike. When rolling initiative, the Lunar may spend motes of Essence to improve her initiative rating, 1 mote buying a +1 modifier to a maximum of the Lunar's Dexterity score.
notes: Unarmed Combat I tree; description continues onto the next page (printed 137/PDF 140).

name: Tyrant Lizard Strike
summary: Lets the Lunar instinctively perceive Essence flows in a target, guiding his blows through defenses for incredibly accurate attacks.
requirements: Minimum Dexterity 2; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: Sinuous Striking Grace.
mechanics: By means of this Charm, a Lunar can instinctively perceive the flows of Essence in his target, using the Exalt's blows through his victim's defenses, making the claws and teeth incredibly accurate. For each mote of Essence spent on this Charm, the Lunar gains an additional attack die on a single unarmed Brawl or Martial Arts attack. This bonus die may not exceed the character's Dexterity.
notes: Unarmed Combat I tree.

name: Snake Body Technique
summary: Lets the Lunar use a civilized enemy's own strength against him by reflecting attacks back before damage is rolled.
requirements: Minimum Dexterity 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Sinuous Striking Grace.
mechanics: By utilizing the sinuous movements of a snake, the Lunar can use a civilized enemy's strengths against him. When attacked by a Melee or Martial Arts attack, before damage is rolled, the Exalt's player can make a reflexive Dexterity + Dodge roll against a difficulty equal to the number of successes rolled on the attack. If the roll succeeds, any damage from the attacker is applied to the attacker instead, with extra successes by the Lunar increasing the number of damage dice. Even if the Exalt fails to reflect the attack, the Lunar's successes on the Dexterity + Dodge roll still reduce the attack's successes normally. The Snake Body Technique is a form of dodge and cannot be used against undodgeable attacks, nor can it be used to avoid counterattack-type effects.
notes: Unarmed Combat I tree.

name: Coiled Cobra Stance
summary: By holding his body in anticipation of the opponent's actions, the Lunar readies a devastating blow against a foe.
requirements: Minimum Dexterity 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Snake Body Technique, Deadly Viper Strike (from the Unarmed Combat II tree).
mechanics: The Lunar activates the Charm before rolling initiative and chooses a self-inflicted penalty to that initiative roll. For every point of penalty on the initiative roll, the Lunar gains a bonus die to his attack roll against the foe; this bonus cannot exceed the Exalted's Dexterity, counts against the Exalted's Charm dice, and only applies during turns when the Lunar plans to make Brawl or Martial Arts attacks. If the Lunar does not act in the turn the Charm is activated, the advantages of the Coiled Cobra Stance are lost. If the Lunar fully dodges or aborts to a parry, the effects of the Coiled Cobra Stance are also lost. Coiled Cobra Stance cannot be used in a Combo with Charms that grant extra actions. A character cannot split his dice pool in a turn when he uses the Coiled Cobra Stance.
notes: Unarmed Combat I tree. Its second prerequisite, Deadly Viper Strike, belongs to the Unarmed Combat II tree and has not been inventoried yet, so it is named only in this row's requirements text rather than as a crossReferences id (which would fail the audit as unresolved).

name: Hydra Head Attack
summary: Enhances the Lunar's reactions, letting him attack multiple times in a turn.
requirements: Minimum Dexterity 3; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: Tyrant Lizard Strike.
mechanics: A skilled Lunar can use Essence to enhance his reactions, giving him preternatural reflexes and allowing him to attack multiple times in a turn. For every 3 motes of Essence spent activating this Charm, the Lunar gains an additional unarmed Brawl or Martial Arts attack. The Lunar can buy no more extra actions with permanent Essence, no more than (the character's Essence + 3, rounded down) this Charm normally means (the character's Essence + 3), but Lunars with lower Essence may lose their ability to make extra actions.
compatibility: Duration: Extra action. Type: Extra action.
notes: Unarmed Combat I tree. The rendered page's cap-formula wording was awkward/possibly OCR-damaged in the printed original around 'the character's Essence + 3' — re-verify exact wording against the physical page before promotion.

name: Deadly Claw Blow
summary: Lets the Lunar convert Dexterity dice into automatic successes on a single unarmed attack, targeting even dematerialized spirits.
requirements: Minimum Dexterity 2; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: Body Weapon Technique.
mechanics: This Charm allows the Lunar to harness his bestial prowess to become a killing machine. He becomes instinctively aware of an opponent's weak spots and how to exploit them, allowing him to target his attacks to maximum effect. He may spend Essence to turn his Dexterity dice into automatic successes when making a single unarmed Brawl or Martial Arts attack. The dice converted into automatic successes are not rolled as part of his dice pool but the remaining dice (including Ability dice and any Attribute dice not converted to successes) are rolled normally. Each Attribute die converted costs 2 motes of Essence. The precision of the Deadly Claw Blow allows the Lunar to harm beings not wholly in the material world, allowing him to target spirits even if they are dematerialized.
notes: Unarmed Combat I tree terminal Charm; also the root of the Unarmed Combat II tree (Claws of the Silver Moon).

name: Claws of the Silver Moon
summary: Temporarily transforms the Lunar's claws and fangs into moonsilver, drastically improving her combat abilities.
requirements: Minimum Stamina 2; Minimum Essence 1; Prerequisite Charms: Deadly Claw Blow.
mechanics: Using this technique, the Lunar temporarily transforms his claws and fangs into moonsilver, drastically improving his combat abilities. When using the Charm, the Lunar may make unarmed claw attacks with his Brawl or Martial Arts at Spd +6, Acc +1, Dmg +3L, Pry +1. He may make unarmed bite attacks with those Abilities at Spd +0, Acc +2, Dmg +5L, Pry +0. Claws of the Silver Moon can harm spirits even if they are dematerialized, and Charms that enhance moonsilver weapons may be used in conjunction with Claws of the Silver Moon.
notes: Unarmed Combat II tree root Charm.

name: Scimitar Claw Technique
summary: Focuses Essence in the Lunar's claws and teeth, enlarging and reshaping them into vicious rending weapons.
requirements: Minimum Manipulation 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Claws of the Silver Moon.
mechanics: Focusing Essence in his claws and teeth, not only does the Lunar transform his claws and teeth into moonsilver, but he also enlarges and reshapes them into vicious rending weapons capable of disemboweling an ill-prepared foe. When using the Charm, the Lunar's claw attacks are Spd +6, Acc +4, Dmg +5L, Pry +4. The Lunar's bite attacks are Spd +3, Acc +2, Dmg +8L, Pry +0. Charms that enhance moonsilver weapons may be used in conjunction with the Scimitar Claw Technique. Claws created with the Scimitar Claw Technique can harm dematerialized spirits.
notes: Unarmed Combat II tree; description begins at the bottom of printed p. 138 (PDF 141) and continues onto printed p. 139 (PDF 142).

name: Adder Fang Method
summary: Lets Lunars enhance their attacks with venom by momentarily generating poison glands or ducts.
requirements: Minimum Stamina 3; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Claws of the Silver Moon.
mechanics: Lunars who know the Adder Fang Method can enhance their attacks with venom. The Charm momentarily creates poison generating glands or ducts, releasing toxins whenever the Lunar successfully makes an unarmed Brawl or Martial Arts bite attack. In addition to the normal damage of the attack, if the target takes damage, she suffers an additional number of dice of lethal damage equal to the Stamina + Essence of the Lunar. This damage is soaked separately and does not add extra successes. However, it ignores the target's armor — only Stamina and other natural soak apply.
notes: Unarmed Combat II tree.

name: Burning Saliva Attack
summary: Lets the Lunar channel Essence into his digestive system, transforming his stomach acids into a lethal ranged weapon.
requirements: Minimum Dexterity 4; Minimum Essence 2; Prerequisite Charms: Adder Fang Method.
mechanics: Using this Charm, a Lunar channels Essence into his digestive system, momentarily transforming his stomach acids into a lethal weapon. He can spit this corrosive phlegm at a target within 10 yards. The attack uses Dexterity + Thrown or Athletics with a -1 accuracy modifier. The opponent may dodge but cannot parry. The attack inflicts 8L + extra successes. The Burning Saliva Attack continues to harm the opponent each turn until it is washed off or otherwise removed. Scraping the acid off requires a Dexterity + Athletics roll and is not a reflexive action — the victim or one of his associates must use a dice action to do so, though she need not roll. Rather than directly attacking an enemy with his acid saliva, the Lunar can target the opponent's weapon. The accuracy of such attacks is -2, and rather than the opponent soaking the damage, her weapon must do so. Its soak is equal to its damage value (so a straight sword that inflicts +3L has a soak of 3). Roll unsoaked damage dice normally, and every two successes reduce the weapon's damage value by one. If the weapon's damage reaches 0, the weapon is rendered useless. The acid continues to harm the weapon.
notes: Unarmed Combat II tree; description continues onto the next page, not yet rendered/reviewed for this checkpoint.
